orders.text:
AO No. 486 of 2017
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. Naresh Pant, Advocate for the 
appellant. 
Mr. Gaurav Singh, Advocate for the 
applicants/caveartors. 
Three days’ delay has been caused 
in moving this appeal by the insurer￾appellant which has been explained in 
the enclosed affidavit. That apart, such 
meagre delay is not seriously opposed by 
the other party counsel Mr. Gaurav 
Singh. Hence, such delay is hereby 
condoned. 
The appeal is admitted for hearing. 
Claim petition was presented on 
account of the death of Smt. Saroj Devi, 
the mother of claimant no. 1 and mother￾in-law of claimant no. 2. The learned 
counsel of the Insurance Company has 
argued that none of the claimants was 
dependant upon the deceased and that 
apart it has been deposed and expected 
by the PW1-Shri Aadesh Kumar Chauhan 
that they did not suffer any pecuniary 
loss on account of the death of his mother 
in such accident. 
Considering the arguments, I 
admit this appeal and the recovery shall 
remain stayed subject to the deposit of 
Rs. 10 lakhs including compulsory 
statutory amount within four weeks 
before the Tribunal concerned. 
Issue notice to the respondents. 
Steps be taken within three days. 
Call the LCR. 
List this matter soon after the 
service is affected. 
Stay application (CLMA No. 
10365/2017) stands disposed of. 
 
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) 
 24.8.2017
Pooja

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
AO No.486 of 2017
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J (Through V.C.)
1. Mr. Naresh Pant, learned counsel for 
the appellant.
2. Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, learned counsel for 
the respondent.
3. The service is duly affected upon 
respondent No.3-Owner of the vehicle, despite 
this, no one put appearance on his behalf.
4. The counsel for both the parties apprise 
to this Court that even before the MACT, the 
owner of vehicle have not contested the case 
and that is the reason the matter was 
proceeded ex-parte against him, but the 
liability has been fastened upon the 
Insurance Company.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant 
submits that at the time of the accident, the 
Driver of the vehicle was not having valid 
Driving License, therefore, in view of the 
judgment of Hon’ble Apex Court in the Case 
of Gohar Mohammad versus Uttar Pradesh 
State Road Transport Corporation and 
Others, (2023) 4 SCC, 381, the liability can 
only be imposed upon the owner of the 
vehicle.
6. In the present proceeding, the owner of 
the vehicle is deliberately avoiding to 
participate, therefore, in such an eventuality 
there is no option except to issue a Bailable 
Warrant against the respondent No.3.
7. The CJM concerned is directed to 
execute the Bailable Warrant.
8. List this matter on 07.10.2025.
9. The Registry is directed to communicate 
about this order to the CJM concerned. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 03.09.2025
R.Bisht
